Asad M.

You asked whether it's relevant. The thing that kills every stack profile site is staleness, because mine would be accurate for about three weeks and then sit there lying about a tool I dropped, and I'm not coming back to edit it. The MCP server is the most interesting thing here and it's the last four words of your description, since that's the one path where the profile updates itself instead of nagging me. I'd make reading a repo or a package file the default way a stack gets built and leave manual entry as the fallback.

Sergei Gordeichuk
Stackness

Stackness

Hi @asadmalik901 !

Thanks a lot for the feedback, I really appreciate that. I'm totally agree that MCP server feature should be prominent, I'll probably move it higher in all descriptions :) [...] And I fully agree that having stack profile up-to-date is one of the main challenge, that's why there're multiple ways to automate that on Stackness. I also plan to publish skills on GitHub to make it even easier to plug in their setup.

Reading the repo or package file is a nice idea, although I'm worried that many people don't share that stuff publicly and scanning them would be complicated. Their AI tools on the other hand can do that and upload things themself :) I'll give it another thought to make it more convenient, thanks again for the feedback!

results.title: 25 Developer Tools I Wish I Knew When I Started Coding 🚀
results.content:
### Comparison with Alternatives

Copilot Chat vs ChatGPT: Copilot Chat has IDE context—it sees your open files and can reference specific code. ChatGPT is more general but requires copying code snippets. Use Copilot Chat for code-specific questions, ChatGPT for broader conceptual discussions.

AI Assistants vs Stack Overflow: Stack Overflow provides vetted, upvoted answers from real developers. AI generates answers that might be wrong. Always verify AI suggestions, especially for security-critical code.

### Common Mistakes Beginners Make

Trusting AI answers blindly leads to bugs. AI generates plausible-sounding code that might have subtle errors. Always review and test generated code. [...] ### Comparison with Alternatives

GitHub vs GitLab: GitHub has the larger community and better social features (stars, forks, contributions graph). GitLab offers free private repos with unlimited collaborators and built-in CI/CD minutes. If you're building open-source, GitHub's network effect matters. For private corporate work, GitLab's free tier is hard to beat.

Git vs SVN: SVN is centralized—you need server access to commit or view history. Git works offline. In 2025, there's little reason to use SVN unless you're maintaining legacy systems.

### Common Mistakes Beginners Make [...] Leverage Docker Compose for local development. Define your entire stack (web server, database, cache, queues) in one `docker-compose.yml`. Start everything with `docker-compose up`. Stop everything with `docker-compose down`.

Pin dependency versions. Specify exact image tags (`postgres:14.2`) instead of `postgres:latest`. "Latest" is a moving target that breaks reproducibility.
